ambiguities: Several generic declarations display 'LocalDef009' as a universe-level name. In those positions it is a universe parameter, not the real-valued model projection D009.

Some standard-library implementations terminate at the supplied frontier, including the private loop used by Fin.foldl. Their standard mathematical meanings are used; their deeper implementations and the target proof are not supplied.
The arithmetic model specifies real-valued operations satisfying error axioms, not a particular floating-point format, rounding rule, or treatment of overflow and underflow.

The factor inequality minimizes the numerical quantity sum_i(factors(i)−1) under the stated product constraint. The target does not define an algorithm for unequal factors or assert that the uniform algorithm minimizes actual numerical error.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the computed result whose absolute error is bounded in the first conjunct.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every arithmetic model fp and natural numbers b and l, defines T(fp,b,l,v) for v:Fin(b^l)→R recursively. At l=0, T(fp,b,0,v)=v(0). At l+1, form w(j)=T(fp,b,l,i↦v(j*b^l+i)) for j∈Fin(b), then return the sequential modeled sum S(fp,b,w) defined in D010. Thus each node sums its b contiguous child blocks in index order.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The first conjunct universally quantifies over all members of this model type; its stored axioms are implicit restrictions on that quantifier.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the exact error coefficient gamma_fp(t*(b−1)). Under the target's admissibility hypothesis its denominator is positive.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The first conjunct assumes this predicate at n=t*(b−1), so ((t*(b−1):N):R)*u_fp<1.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Specifies all assumptions built into fp. The summation uses the addition operation, its relative-error bound, and its exact left-zero law; the other operation axioms restrict the model type but do not appear in the summation algorithm.
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs a model from u∈R with 0≤u; functions A,S,M,D:R×R→R and Q:R→R; the law ∀x∈R, A(0,x)=x; and the following axioms. For every x,y∈R there exists δ∈R with |δ|≤u and A(x,y)=(x+y)(1+δ). Separately, for every x,y there exists such a δ with S(x,y)=(x−y)(1+δ), and separately with M(x,y)=(xy)(1+δ). For every x,y with y≠0 there exists such a δ with D(x,y)=(x/y)(1+δ). For every x≥0 there exists such a δ with Q(x)=sqrt(x)(1+δ). Each existential error may depend on its operation and operands; no common δ is required. D is unconstrained by its error axiom at y=0, and Q at x<0.
dependency_coverage.name: Arithmetic model constructor and axioms

binders: Universally quantify t,b∈N, in that order, and assume 0<t and 0<b.
In the first conjunct, universally quantify an arithmetic model fp; assuming ((t*(b−1):N):R)*u_fp<1, universally quantify v:Fin(b^t)→R.
Independently, in the second conjunct, universally quantify factors:Fin(t)→N; assume ∀i∈Fin(t), 0<factors(i), and then assume product_{i∈Fin(t)} factors(i)=b^t.
The last two conjuncts have no additional binders or hypotheses beyond t,b and their positivity.
conclusions: For every fp satisfying ((t*(b−1):N):R)*u_fp<1 and every v:Fin(b^t)→R, |T(fp,b,t,v)−sum_{i=0}^{b^t−1} v(i)| ≤ gamma_fp(t*(b−1))*sum_{i=0}^{b^t−1}|v(i)|.
For every positive natural factor vector factors of length t with product b^t, t*(b−1) ≤ sum_{i=0}^{t−1}(factors(i)−1), as an inequality in N.
sum_{i=0}^{t−1}(b−1)=t*(b−1), as an equality in N.
These four statements are asserted jointly, with conjunction structure C1 ∧ (C2 ∧ (C3 ∧ C4)); the factor statements do not depend on fp, v or the admissibility hypothesis.
hypotheses: t and b are strictly positive natural numbers. No assumption b≥2 is imposed.
The model fp contains u_fp≥0, binary real operations A_fp, S_fp, M_fp, D_fp, and a unary real operation Q_fp.

For every pair x,y∈R, each of A_fp(x,y), S_fp(x,y), and M_fp(x,y) equals its corresponding exact result x+y, x−y, or x*y, multiplied by 1+δ for some real δ with |δ|≤u_fp. The witnesses are separate and may depend on the operation and operands.
For every x,y∈R with y≠0, D_fp(x,y)=(x/y)*(1+δ) for some δ with |δ|≤u_fp. For every x∈R with x≥0, Q_fp(x)=sqrt(x)*(1+δ) for some δ with |δ|≤u_fp.
Only the first conjunct additionally requires ((t*(b−1):N):R)*u_fp<1. The input vector may have arbitrary real entries, including mixed signs.
Only the factor inequality additionally requires every factors(i)>0 and product_i factors(i)=b^t.
mathematical_definitions: Fin(n)={0,...,n−1}. All displayed sums and products range over the entire indicated finite index type and use exact natural or real arithmetic.
Natural subtraction is truncated at zero. Under b>0 and factors(i)>0, b−1 and factors(i)−1 coincide with their ordinary nonnegative integer differences.
For n∈N, gamma_fp(n)=((n:R)*u_fp)/(1−(n:R)*u_fp), and admissibility at n means (n:R)*u_fp<1. The target uses n=t*(b−1).
For a vector w:Fin(n)→R, define S(fp,n,w) by s0=0, s_(k+1)=A_fp(s_k,w(k)) for k=0,...,n−1, and S(fp,n,w)=s_n.
For every b,l∈N and v:Fin(b^l)→R, define T(fp,b,0,v)=v(0). For depth l+1, define v_j(i)=v(j*b^l+i) for j∈Fin(b), i∈Fin(b^l), and T(fp,b,l+1,v)=S(fp,b,j↦T(fp,b,l,v_j)).

The base vector has length b^0=1. A node at depth l+1 partitions its input into b contiguous blocks of length b^l, recursively sums each block, and sequentially adds the child results starting from zero.
|x| is ordinary real absolute value. The error measure is absolute scalar error, and sum_i|v(i)| is the input vector's l1 norm; there is no division by the exact sum.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive depth t and positive branching factor b, recursively summing b^t arbitrary real inputs with b contiguous children per node and sequential modeled addition at each node has absolute error at most gamma_fp(t*(b−1)) times the sum of the input magnitudes, for every supplied arithmetic model satisfying t*(b−1)*u_fp<1. Independently, among all t positive natural factors whose product is b^t, the sum of the factors minus one is at least t*(b−1). Taking every factor equal to b has product b^t and attains this cost exactly.

vacuity_risks: The outer implication makes no claim at t=0 or b=0; those cases are excluded by the positivity hypotheses.
For a particular model failing t*(b−1)*u_fp<1, the first conjunct's implication is vacuous. This does not affect the separate factor statements.
The model type is not forced to be empty: exact real operations with u=0 satisfy the supplied axioms and admissibility for every finite count.
The factor constraint is satisfiable for every allowed t,b by taking every factor equal to b, as explicitly certified by the last two conjuncts.

When b=1, the count t*(b−1) is zero and admissibility holds for every model regardless of u. The single input passes unchanged through every level by A_fp(0,x)=x, so the bound is zero. Positive factors with product 1 are all 1, so the factor inequality also reduces to equality.
When u_fp=0, modeled addition is exact and the error coefficient is zero. An all-zero input also makes the error bound zero. These are valid degenerate cases.

Although gamma is defined even when its denominator vanishes because Lean real division is total, the first conjunct's strict admissibility hypothesis ensures that its denominator is positive; the target does not obtain a bound through division by zero.
